title: Migrate model records to metadata v1 (backfill + rollback plan)
author: Michael Nguyen
release_notes: No customer-visible behavior change intended. Adds metadata_v1 storage + backfill and keeps legacy fields readable during rollout.
body: Context: As part of the model metadata schema v1 rollout (see pr-18421), we need to migrate existing model/variant records so the registry can serve metadata_v1 consistently and unblock changelog generation + Console change history. Today, key fields are split across legacy columns and ad-hoc JSON; some records are incomplete and some are deployment-specific. This PR introduces a forward-only schema migration, a backfill job, and an explicit rollback procedure that preserves read-compatibility during the rollout window. Summary of changes: 1) DB schema: add metadata_v1 columns (jsonb) for model_versions and model_variants, plus schema_hash and migration bookkeeping (backfilled_at, backfill_source, backfill_warnings). Add partial indexes for common queries (model_id + version, availability filters). 2) Backfill job: new admin command `registry-admin backfill-metadata-v1` that transforms legacy fields into metadata v1 shape using the v1 schema library. Supports dry-run, batching, concurrency=1 by default, and idempotency (safe to re-run). Emits structured logs and counters per phase. 3) Safety checks: the backfill performs validation against the v1 JSON Schema, with strict vs permissive modes. Strict mode fails the run; permissive mode writes metadata_v1 plus warning annotations and a reason code. Includes a blocklist for known-bad legacy records (write no-op + emit alert) so we don’t half-migrate. 4) Read path compatibility: the registry read API continues to serve legacy fields, and adds `metadata_v1` on the response when present. No consumers are switched in this PR. A feature flag `MODEL_METADATA_V1_READ_PREFERRED` (default false) is included for staging-only verification. 5) Rollback plan: documented steps to revert reads to legacy-only, and to remove/ignore partially written metadata_v1 safely. Because the migration is additive, rollback is primarily a configuration rollback; the backfill writes can remain without impacting existing callers. Implementation details: Mapping logic is in `internal/metadata/migrate/legacy_to_v1.ts` and is intentionally conservative: (a) version: derives `version.semver` if present; otherwise sets `version.scheme=registry-seq` and preserves the legacy version string in `internal.legacy_version`. (b) tokenizer/runtime: best-effort inference from existing model_family + engine fields; if unknown, sets `compatibility.requires_human_review=true` and adds a warning. (c) availability: populates Hosted/Dedicated/Private availability based on legacy deployment flags and region allowlists; defaults to "unknown" rather than assuming global availability. (d) deprecations: carries forward existing deprecation_date fields; if only a free-form note exists, it is placed under internal.deprecation_context and not made public. Metrics/monitoring added: `model_registry.metadata_v1.backfill.records_total` (tagged by entity=model_version|variant, result=written|skipped|failed), `model_registry.metadata_v1.backfill.validation_failures_total` (tagged by reason), `model_registry.metadata_v1.backfill.duration_ms` (per batch), and `model_registry.metadata_v1.backfill.warnings_total` (tagged by warning_code). Also adds a one-time gauge report in logs at end-of-run: counts by model_family and deployment mode to help spot skew. Ops runbook (included in this PR): - Recommended rollout sequence: (1) deploy additive schema; (2) run backfill in staging with dry-run + strict mode; (3) run staging with strict write; (4) enable `MODEL_METADATA_V1_READ_PREFERRED` in staging and compare API diffs; (5) run production backfill in permissive mode with alerting; (6) follow up on warnings and re-run strict mode for clean-up. - Batch sizing guidance: start with 500 records/batch, pause between batches if DB CPU > 65% for 5m. - Alert thresholds: if failed > 0.5% in any 10m window or validation_failures spikes, page. - Success criteria: 99.9% records written or intentionally skipped with known warning codes; 0 schema validation failures in strict mode after remediation. Rollback steps (documented under `docs/ops/metadata-v1-migration.md`): 1) Disable `MODEL_METADATA_V1_READ_PREFERRED` everywhere (or confirm it remains false). 2) Stop/rollback any downstream consumers that switched to metadata_v1 reads (none in this PR). 3) If the backfill is causing DB load, stop the job; already-written metadata_v1 is safe to keep. 4) If we must revert writes, run `registry-admin backfill-metadata-v1 --revert` which clears metadata_v1 only for records written by this job (checks backfill_source and backfilled_at window), leaving any manual edits intact. 5) Post-rollback: export warning/failure report to Slack #eng-releases and attach to ENG-9822 for follow-up. Testing: Adds unit tests for legacy->v1 mapping for common model families and known edge cases (missing tokenizer, non-semver versions, quantization variants). Adds an integration test that runs the backfill against a seeded test DB and verifies idempotency and performance (bounded queries, no full table scans). Includes a regression test for the case raised in SUP-28429 (need exact change history later) by ensuring we preserve legacy identifiers in internal fields for traceability. Notes for reviewers: - The goal here is correctness + safety, not perfect metadata completeness. We prefer warnings over guessing. - Please focus on: (a) DB migration safety (locks/index builds), (b) idempotency + revert correctness, and (c) whether warning codes are actionable for follow-up. - Connor: release train implications are in the runbook; this should land before we turn on CI schema-diff checks in other repos.
commits: db(migrations): add metadata_v1 columns + indexes for model records
admin(backfill): implement legacy_to_v1 transform + idempotent writer
validation: run JSON Schema validation with strict/permissive modes
ops: add rollback/revert command and migration runbook
metrics: emit counters/timers for backfill health + warnings
tests: mapping fixtures + seeded DB integration test
ci_checks: migration safety check (no long exclusive locks): pass
review_conversation: Quentin Harris (review): Mapping looks reasonable, but I’m worried about silently synthesizing semver for legacy versions. Can we make sure we never fabricate a semver when the legacy field is non-semver? Also, can you include a warning code for "version_non_semver" so we can chase those down before we expose public release notes? Michael Nguyen (author): Agreed. I removed the "try to coerce" path. If legacy version doesn’t match semver, we set version.scheme=registry-seq and stash legacy string in internal.legacy_version + emit warning_code=version_non_semver. Added tests for a couple known offenders. Ethan Park (review): DB migration: are the new indexes created concurrently? We’ve been burned by blocking writes on large tables. Also, the integration test uses `CREATE INDEX` without CONCURRENTLY; can we keep prod migration safe? Michael Nguyen (author): Yes—prod migration uses `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` where allowed; for the one partial index that can’t be concurrent in our migration framework, I added a follow-up to build it out-of-band and left it out of the migration. Updated docs with the exact commands. Connor O'Brien (review): Rollback plan is good; can you add a clear "stop conditions" section and who to page if validation failures exceed threshold? Also please ensure the revert command only clears rows written by this job (don’t wipe manual edits). Michael Nguyen (author): Added stop conditions + paging instructions (Release Eng on-call, then Platform DB on-call). Revert checks backfill_source=="metadata_v1_backfill_v1" and backfilled_at within provided window; it refuses to run without both. Sahana Iyer (review): CI: the seeded DB integration test initially failed on my branch due to timing/flake. Can we reduce batch size in tests and add deterministic ordering? Michael Nguyen (author): Done—test uses batch_size=50 and orders by primary key; also added retry around transient connection reset in CI. Re-ran CI 3x. Quentin Harris (approval): Approved after warning code changes + semver handling fix. Ethan Park (approval): Approved; thanks for addressing index safety. Connor O'Brien (approval): Approved; runbook is clear enough to hand to the release train.
